source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Suctioning carrying fairly little established risk of introducing any infection into the client's lower airway","B":"The suction catheter directly enters the lower airway, a normally sterile area, so introducing pathogens could cause serious respiratory infection","C":"Clean technique being considered just as effective and acceptable as sterile technique for this particular invasive procedure","D":"Sterile technique being needed only for the client's very first suctioning session, rather than for every subsequent one"}}
source_row.rationale: Sterile suctioning technique is required because the suction catheter directly enters the lower airway, a normally sterile area, so introducing pathogens through non-sterile technique could cause serious respiratory infection, a consideration applicable to every suctioning episode, not only the first.
source_row.source_name: AARC — Endotracheal Suctioning Clinical Practice Guideline
